simple.meaning: פָּטוּר (pâṭûwr) is a Hebrew action word meaning “opened , i.e. (as noun) a bud.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in 1 Kings, beginning at 1 Kings 6:18. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּטוּר (H6358) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: פָּטוּר (pâṭûwr) / H6358 is traced through 1 Kings 6:18, 1 Kings 6:29, 1 Kings 6:32, 1 Kings 6:35 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: There was cedar on the house within, carved with buds and open flowers. All was cedar. No stone was visible.
He carved all the walls of the house around with carved figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, inside and outside.
So he made two doors of olive wood; and he carved on them carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold. He spread the gold on the cherubim and on the palm trees.
He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers; and he overlaid them with gold fitted on the engraved work.
